chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a traveling man upon whom death descended, so he gave money to a man from the merchants, saying to him, 'This money is so-and-so's son of so-and-so; I have neither little nor much in it, so deliver it to him; he may spend it wherever he wishes.' He died and did not command his partner, whom he had appointed for him, with any specific instruction, and his partner does not know what motivated him to do so. How should he act? He said, 'He places it wherever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a dying traveler who entrusts money to a merchant with general instructions?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the legal principle of *ikhtiyar* (discretion) is applied to a deathbed bequest (*mawdūʿ*) where the testator grants the trustee broad authority to allocate the funds as he sees fit. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between specific bequests and those allowing discretionary distribution, emphasizing the trustee's autonomy in the absence of further constraints. It serves as a key precedent in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for understanding the flexibility of estate management in cases of ambiguous or open-ended instructions.
